Scotland's Best Campsites for Motorcycle Tourers

Scotland is one of the best countries in Europe for motorcycle camping. The right to roam means wild camping is legal on most unenclosed land, and formal campsites range from basic Highland pitches to well-equipped sites with hot showers and drying rooms. Camping extends your range, reduces your costs, and puts you closer to the landscape.

Wild Camping

Scotland's Land Reform Act gives you the right to camp on most unenclosed land, provided you follow the Scottish Outdoor Access Code. This means you can pitch a tent beside a Highland loch, in a mountain glen, or on a quiet beach — legally and for free. Key rules:

  • Camp away from buildings and roads
  • Use a small tent, leave no trace
  • Don't camp in the same place for more than 2-3 nights
  • Respect wildlife and other land users
  • Take all rubbish with you

Highland Campsites

Sango Sands, Durness — NC500 favourite with pitches overlooking a stunning white sand beach. Basic but spectacular. The views north across the Pentland Firth to Orkney are mesmerising.

Applecross Campsite — At the foot of the Bealach na Bà, with views across the Sound of Raasay to Skye. Basic but well-maintained. Walk to the Applecross Inn for dinner.

Red Squirrel Campsite, Glen Coe — Set among mature pines with the mountains looming all around. Good facilities including a bar with real ales. Popular with bikers, walkers, and climbers.

Wild camping in the Scottish Highlands is one of motorcycling's great pleasures. Pitching your tent beside a loch as the sun sets over the mountains — it doesn't get better than this.

More Recommended Sites

  • Camusdarach, Arisaig — White sand beach campsite on the Road to the Isles, views to Rum and Eigg
  • Invercaimbe, Arisaig — Tiny, peaceful site near the beach with stunning sunset views
  • Lickisto Blackhouse, Harris — Outer Hebrides campsite beside a restored blackhouse, wild Atlantic views
  • Ardnamurchan Campsite — Remote peninsula site near Britain's most westerly point
  • Lazy Duck, Nethy Bridge — Boutique Cairngorms campsite in mature woodland
  • Comrie Croft, Perthshire — Eco-friendly site with mountain bike trails and a community feel

Camping Gear Tips for Motorcyclists

Space is at a premium on a motorcycle. Choose a lightweight 2-person tent (allows room for gear inside), a compact sleeping bag rated to 0°C for Scotland, and a self-inflating mat. A compact stove (MSR PocketRocket or similar) and a single pot cover most cooking needs. Pack gear in dry bags inside soft panniers. Scottish camping demands midges repellent (Smidge brand is most effective) from June to September.
keyTakeaways: Scotland's Land Reform Act makes wild camping legal on most unenclosed land, provided you follow the Scottish Outdoor Access Code and leave no trace.
NC500 favourites like Sango Sands at Durness and Applecross Campsite pair basic facilities with spectacular beach and sea-loch settings.
Red Squirrel Campsite in Glen Coe is a biker favourite with a bar and real ales set among mature pines.
Pack a lightweight 2-person tent, a sleeping bag rated to 0C and midge repellent (Smidge is most effective) for June to September.
Do not camp in the same wild spot for more than two or three nights, and always camp away from buildings and roads.

faq.q: Is wild camping legal in Scotland?
faq.a: Yes. Scotland's Land Reform Act gives you the right to camp on most unenclosed land, provided you follow the Scottish Outdoor Access Code. You can legally pitch a small tent beside a Highland loch, in a mountain glen or on a quiet beach for free. Camp away from buildings and roads, leave no trace and take all rubbish with you.

faq.q: How long can I stay in one wild camping spot?
faq.a: The Scottish Outdoor Access Code advises against camping in the same place for more than two or three nights. Move on regularly, use a small tent, respect wildlife and other land users, and always leave the site exactly as you found it. This keeps wild camping sustainable and welcome across the Highlands.

faq.q: Which campsites are best for the NC500?
faq.a: Sango Sands at Durness is a firm NC500 favourite, with pitches overlooking a stunning white sand beach and views north across the Pentland Firth to Orkney. Applecross Campsite sits at the foot of the Bealach na Ba with views to Skye, and you can walk to the Applecross Inn for dinner.

faq.q: What camping gear suits a motorcycle tour of Scotland?
faq.a: Space is limited, so choose a lightweight 2-person tent for room to store gear inside, a compact sleeping bag rated to 0C, and a self-inflating mat. A small stove such as an MSR PocketRocket and a single pot cover most cooking. Pack everything in dry bags inside soft panniers, and carry midge repellent.

faq.q: When are midges a problem in Scotland?
faq.a: Midges are at their worst from June to September, particularly in sheltered areas near water at dawn and dusk. They can make camping miserable if you are unprepared, so carry an effective repellent (Smidge is widely rated as the best) and consider a head net. Breezy, exposed pitches tend to see fewer midges.
